title: 4-bit Johnson Counter
statement: Implement a 4-bit Johnson counter that rotates inverted feedback through the register. On each clock edge the MSB is fed back inverted into the LSB, producing eight unique states. A synchronous reset should return the counter to 0000.
module_signature: module johnson_counter_4bit(input clk, input rst, output reg [3:0] q);
behavior: q cycles through eight unique states with inverted feedback.
Updates occur only on clock edges.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Do not use memory arrays or asynchronous logic.
hint: Implement the register as a shift register with inverted MSB feedback.
